title: Data Structures and Algorithms
topics: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions
Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: A method performs 2 basic operations for each item of an input of size 400. How many operations does it carry out in all?
items.s: The work is 2 operations per item times 400 items, that is 800 operations.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A method needs one 16 byte record for each of the 5000 items of its input. How much storage does the working copy occupy, in bytes?
items.s: The copy holds 5000 records of 16 bytes, that is 80000 bytes.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: An array of 2 byte elements begins at address 2000. What is the address of the element with index 21?
items.s: The address is base + index x element size = 2000 + 21 x 2 = 2042.

items.q: A simulation performs 1000 operations; 60 per cent of them push and the rest pop. How many pushes occur?
items.s: The pushes are 60/100 x 1000 = 600 operations.

items.q: A stack is held in a block of 1000 bytes and each item occupies 4 bytes. How many items can it hold?
items.s: The block holds 1000/4 = 250 items.

items.q: Keys are placed in a table of 47 positions by taking the remainder of the key on division by 47. At which position does the key 745 land?
items.s: The remainder of 745 on division by 47 is 40.

items.q: An undirected graph has 12 vertices and no two are joined by more than one edge. What is the largest number of edges it can have?
items.s: Every vertex can reach the other n - 1, so the edges number 12 x 11 / 2 = 66.

items.q: Bubble sort is applied to an array of 10 items that happens to be in reverse order, so no pass ends early. How many comparisons are made?
items.s: The passes compare 10 - 1, then 10 - 2 and so on, which adds to n(n-1)/2 = 45.

items.q: Binary search is applied to a sorted array of 1023 items. What is the greatest number of comparisons it can make?
items.s: Each comparison halves the range, and the least k with 2^k at least 1023 + 1 is 10.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: A linear search is made for a key that is known to be present in an array of 100 items and every position is equally likely. What is the average number of comparisons?
items.s: The positions need 1 up to 100 comparisons with equal chance, so the average is (100 + 1)/2 = 50.5.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: A nested loop runs an inner block whose cost is 4 operations once for every ordered pair of items in an input of size 60. How many operations are carried out?
items.s: There are n squared = 3600 ordered pairs, each costing 4, so the total is 14400.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A divide and conquer method splits an input of size 128 into halves, spends 2 operations on every item at each level and has 7 levels in all. How many operations does it perform?
items.s: One level costs 2 x 128 = 256 operations and there are 7 levels, giving 1792 operations.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: The naive method for multiplying two 100 by 100 matrices performs two operations for every triple of indices. How many operations does it perform?
items.s: There are n cubed = 1000000 triples and two operations for each, so 2000000 operations.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A loop considers every unordered pair of distinct items drawn from an input of size 50, taking each pair once. How many pairs are examined?
items.s: The pairs number n(n-1)/2, that is 50 x 49 / 2 = 1225.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A two dimensional array with 25 rows and 27 columns of 4 byte elements is stored row by row starting at address 0. What is the address of the element in row 14 and column 21?
items.s: Its position in the block is row x columns + column = 399, so the address is 0 + 399 x 4 = 1596.

items.q: A singly linked chain holds 5000 nodes, each carrying a 12 byte item and a pointer of 4 bytes. How many bytes of storage does the chain occupy?
items.s: Each node takes 12 + 4 = 16 bytes, so 5000 nodes take 80000 bytes.

items.q: A doubly linked chain holds 200 nodes, each carrying a 16 byte item and two pointers of 4 bytes. How many bytes of storage does the chain occupy?
items.s: Each node takes 16 + 8 = 24 bytes, so the whole chain takes 4800 bytes.

items.q: A chain of 500 nodes is walked from the head to the node in position 250, counting the head as position one. How many nodes are passed through?
items.s: The walk stops at position 250 having passed through exactly 250 nodes.

items.q: An item is to be inserted into a sorted array of 1000 elements at index 61. How many existing elements must be moved one place to the right?
items.s: Every element from index 61 onwards shifts, which is 1000 - 61 = 939 elements.

items.q: A circular queue uses 16 cells and its rear index currently stands at 0. After 5 further insertions, which index holds the rear?
items.s: Each insertion advances the index by one and wraps at 16, so (0 + 5) mod 16 = 5.

items.q: A balanced expression contains 8 opening brackets and the same number of closing brackets. If every closing bracket causes one pop, how many pop operations occur?
items.s: Each closing bracket matches one opening one, so exactly 8 pops are performed.

items.q: The postfix expression 6 9 - is evaluated with a stack. What result is left on the stack?
items.s: The two values are pushed and the operator - combines them, giving 6 - 9 = -3.

items.q: A binary tree of height 3 is as full as it can be at every level. What is the largest number of nodes it can contain, counting the root as level one?
items.s: A full tree of height h holds 2^h - 1 nodes, so 2^3 - 1 = 7.

items.q: A complete binary tree holds 15 nodes. What is its height, counted as the number of edges on the longest path from the root?
items.s: A complete tree of 15 nodes has floor(log2(15)) = 3 edges on its longest path.

items.q: A binary tree has every level filled to the bottom, where the height is 4 and the root sits at level one. How many leaves does it have?
items.s: The bottom level is level 4 and carries 2^3 = 8 nodes, all of them leaves.

items.q: A full binary tree holds 15 nodes in all. How many of them are internal, that is not leaves?
items.s: A full binary tree of n nodes has (n - 1)/2 internal nodes, so (15 - 1)/2 = 7.

items.q: Keys are inserted into an empty binary search tree in strict increasing order. How many edges are on the longest path from the root when 127 keys have been inserted?
items.s: Every key becomes the right child of the one before it, so the tree is a chain with 127 - 1 = 126 edges.

items.q: An inorder traversal of a binary search tree holding 127 nodes stops as soon as it has visited 1 nodes. How many nodes remain unvisited?
items.s: The traversal has visited 1 of the 127 nodes, so 126 of them are still unvisited.

items.q: In a full binary tree numbered with the root at level one, how many nodes stand on level 3?
items.s: Level one has one node and every level doubles the count, so level 3 holds 2^2 = 4 nodes.

items.q: A balanced binary search tree holds 255 keys. What is the greatest number of nodes examined by one lookup?
items.s: The search follows one node per level, and a balanced tree of 255 keys has 8 levels.

items.q: A binary heap is stored in an array with the root at index 0. What is the index of the parent of the node at index 125?
items.s: The parent of index i sits at (i - 1)/2 rounded down, so (125 - 1)/2 = 62.

items.q: A binary heap is stored in an array with the root at index 0. What is the index of the right child of the node at index 5?
items.s: The left child sits at 2i + 1 and the right at 2i + 2, so 2 x 5 + 2 = 12.

items.q: A heap holds 31 items in an array. What is the height of the tree it forms, counted in edges?
items.s: The tree is complete, so its height is the floor of log2 of the count: floor(log2(31)) = 4.

items.q: An item is sifted up from the bottom of a complete heap holding 128 items. What is the greatest number of exchanges it can take part in?
items.s: One exchange is possible per level and the tree has floor(log2(128)) = 7 levels above the bottom.

items.q: A heap is built by repairing every internal node of a complete tree holding 127 items, from the lowest upwards. How many nodes are repaired?
items.s: The leaves need no repair, and a complete tree of 127 items has 64 of them, leaving 63 internal nodes.

items.q: Heap sort is applied to 16 items. Taking each removal as costing at most 4 sift steps, what is the largest total number of sift steps?
items.s: Each of the 16 removals costs at most 4 steps, so the total is at most 64.

items.q: The largest item of a list of 20 items is found by scanning the list once from the second item onwards. How many comparisons are needed?
items.s: The first item is the running largest and each of the other 19 items is compared with it, so 19 comparisons are made.

items.q: A hash table has 300 positions and holds 60 keys. Calculate its load factor.
items.s: The load factor is keys divided by positions: 60/300 = 0.2.

items.q: A hash table with 100 positions uses chaining and holds 100 keys. Taking the keys as evenly spread as possible, what is the average chain length?
items.s: The keys are shared among 100 positions, so each chain holds 100/100 = 1 keys on average.

items.q: A table of 20 positions uses linear probing. The positions from 9 through 17 are already occupied and the one after them is free. A key whose home position is 9 is inserted. How many probes does it take?
items.s: The occupied run holds 9 positions, so the key probes those 9 and then the free one, taking 10 probes in all.

items.q: A table holds 150 keys and the load factor must not exceed 80 per cent. What is the smallest number of positions that will serve?
items.s: The positions needed satisfy keys/positions at most 80/100, so at least 150 x 100/80 = 188 positions are required.

items.q: A chained hash table holds 2000 keys, each key takes 16 bytes and each chain pointer takes 4 bytes. How many bytes do the key records occupy in all?
items.s: Each record takes 16 + 4 = 20 bytes, so 2000 records take 40000 bytes.

items.q: A directed graph has 5 vertices and at most one arrow from any vertex to any other. What is the largest number of arrows it can have?
items.s: Each of the 5 vertices may point at each of the other 4, so there can be 20 arrows.

items.q: The adjacency matrix of a graph with 100 vertices is stored with 4 byte per entry. How many bytes does the matrix occupy?
items.s: The matrix has 100 x 100 = 10000 entries, which take 40000 bytes.

items.q: An undirected graph with 1000 vertices and 200 edges is stored as adjacency lists, each link taking 4 bytes and each list header taking 4 bytes. How many bytes are needed?
items.s: There are 1000 headers and 2 x 200 = 400 links, so the total is 4000 + 1600 = 5600 bytes.

items.q: A spanning tree is to be formed for a connected graph with 100 vertices. How many edges does the tree contain?
items.s: A tree on 100 vertices always has one edge fewer than vertices, that is 99.

items.q: A breadth first search starts at a vertex that has 5 neighbours, and every later vertex also has 5 neighbours. How many vertices stand on level 2 of the search?
items.s: The front grows by the factor 5 - 1 at each step, so level 2 holds 5 x 4^1 = 20 vertices.

items.q: A graph has 16 vertices and every vertex has degree 5. How many edges does the graph contain?
items.s: The degrees total 16 x 5 = 80, and each edge is counted twice, so there are 40 edges.

items.q: Selection sort is applied to an array of 20 items. How many comparisons does it make, whatever the original order?
items.s: The first scan compares 20 items, the next 19, and so on, giving n(n-1)/2 = 190.

items.q: Insertion sort is applied to an array of 40 items arranged in decreasing order. How many shifts of elements are carried out?
items.s: The worst case shifts 1 + 2 + ... + (40 - 1) elements, which is n(n-1)/2 = 780.

items.q: Merge sort is applied to 16 items. Into how many levels of splitting does the recursion divide the work?
items.s: The array is halved until single items remain, which takes log2(16) = 4 levels.

items.q: Merge sort is applied to 8 items and every level of the recursion does at most 8 comparisons in all. What is the largest total number of comparisons?
items.s: Each of the 3 levels costs at most 8 comparisons, so the total is at most 24.

items.q: A partition about a pivot leaves 2 items to the left of the pivot and 47 to its right in an array of 50 items. The right part is then sorted by a method that compares every pair once. How many comparisons does that part need?
items.s: The right part holds 47 items, so its pair comparisons number m(m-1)/2 = 1081.

items.q: Quick sort takes its worst case on an array of 25 items already in order when the pivot is always the first item. How many comparisons are made?
items.s: Each partition removes one item and compares it with all the rest, giving n(n-1)/2 = 300.

items.q: A sorting method performs n log2 n comparisons on 2000 items. Taking log2 2000 as 10, how many comparisons does it perform?
items.s: The work is 2000 x 10 = 20000 comparisons.

items.q: A radix sort processes 1000 keys and each key is examined once for each of its 3 digits. How many key examinations does the method make?
items.s: Every pass looks at all 1000 keys, and there are 3 passes, so 3000 examinations are made.

items.q: A linear search is made for a key that is absent from an array of 100 items. How many comparisons are needed before the search can report failure?
items.s: Every item is compared before the search can stop, so 100 comparisons are made.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: A recursive method makes 4 calls from every activation and the recursion has depth 3. Counting the first call as level zero, how many activations are created in all?
items.s: The levels hold 1, 4, 4 squared and so on up to 4^3, which adds to 85 activations.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: The unmodified recursive method for the 10th Fibonacci number makes one call for each node of its recursion tree. How many calls does it make in all?
items.s: The tree has 2 x F(11) - 1 nodes, and F(11) = 89, so the calls number 177.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: A recurrence splits an input of size 81 into 3 equal parts and costs nothing outside the recursive calls. How many levels does the tree of calls have?
items.s: The size falls from 81 to one by dividing by 3, which needs log_3(81) = 4 levels.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: Traversal may be defined as
o: the visiting of every item of a structure once in a stated order
the item about which a partition is arranged
a container in which the item put in earliest is the first one taken out
the visiting of both subtrees of a node before the node itself
items.s: Traversal: the visiting of every item of a structure once in a stated order. The other options describe Queue, Pivot, Postorder traversal.

items.q: Which term is described by “the number attached to an item that fixes the order in which it leaves a ranked container”?
o: Heap
Sift up
Heapify
Priority value
items.s: Priority value is the number attached to an item that fixes the order in which it leaves a ranked container.

items.q: Repeated top removal sort may be defined as
o: a two sided limit showing that two functions grow at the same rate up to constant factors
the rebuilding of a table in a larger space with a new rule when it becomes too full
a sorting method that repeatedly takes away the best item of a ranked tree and refills the gap
the exploration of a graph by following one route as far as possible before backing up
items.s: Repeated top removal sort: a sorting method that repeatedly takes away the best item of a ranked tree and refills the gap. The other options describe Big theta notation, Depth first search, Rehashing.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Linear search.
o: a square table whose entry shows whether a pair of points is joined
the distance of a node from the top, counted in edges
the checking of items one after another until the wanted one is found or the list ends
the condition reached when an attempt is made to add to a container that is already full
items.s: Linear search: the checking of items one after another until the wanted one is found or the list ends. The other options describe Adjacency matrix, Overflow, Level.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: Which of the following best describes Backtracking?
o: the abandoning of a partial attempt as soon as it cannot be completed and the trying of another
the handling of a clash by looking for another free position in the same table
the splitting of a problem into parts, the solving of each, and the joining of the results
a task for which no method with polynomial running time is known
items.s: Backtracking: the abandoning of a partial attempt as soon as it cannot be completed and the trying of another. The other options describe Divide and conquer, Open addressing, Hard case.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: The statement “a container in which the item put in earliest is the first one taken out” describes which of the following?
o: Call stack
Pop
Queue
Underflow
items.s: Queue is a container in which the item put in earliest is the first one taken out.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Divide and conquer.
o: a complete tree kept so that every parent outranks both of its children
a container in which the item most recently put in is the first one taken out
the splitting of a problem into parts, the solving of each, and the joining of the results
the handling of a clash by keeping a chain of items at each position
items.s: Divide and conquer: the splitting of a problem into parts, the solving of each, and the joining of the results. The other options describe Stack, Heap, Chaining.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Priority value.
o: an exchange method that repeatedly swaps neighbours that are out of order
the number attached to an item that fixes the order in which it leaves a ranked container
a divide and conquer method that sorts two halves and then interleaves them
a sorting method that repeatedly takes away the best item of a ranked tree and refills the gap
items.s: Priority value: the number attached to an item that fixes the order in which it leaves a ranked container. The other options describe Merge sort, Repeated top removal sort, Bubble sort.

items.q: The statement “the number of stored items divided by the number of positions available” describes which of the following?
o: Load factor
Rehashing
Linear probing
Open addressing
items.s: Load factor is the number of stored items divided by the number of positions available.

items.q: The statement “a method that orders items by processing their digit positions one at a time” describes which of the following?
o: Insertion sort
Counting sort
Merge sort
Radix sort
items.s: Radix sort is a method that orders items by processing their digit positions one at a time.

items.q: The statement “a hierarchy in which every key is larger than all keys to its left and smaller than all to its right” describes which of the following?
o: Ordered lookup tree
Level
Leaf
Postorder traversal
items.s: Ordered lookup tree is a hierarchy in which every key is larger than all keys to its left and smaller than all to its right.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Pivot?
o: the visiting of every item of a structure once in a stated order
a two sided limit showing that two functions grow at the same rate up to constant factors
the condition reached when an attempt is made to remove from a container that holds nothing
the item about which a partition is arranged
items.s: Pivot: the item about which a partition is arranged. The other options describe Underflow, Traversal, Big theta notation.

items.q: Which term is described by “the visiting of a left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree”?
o: Root
Level
Inorder traversal
Binary tree
items.s: Inorder traversal is the visiting of a left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree.

items.q: The statement “the case in which two different keys are sent to the same position” describes which of the following?
o: Clustering
Open addressing
Collision
Chaining
items.s: Collision is the case in which two different keys are sent to the same position.

items.q: The statement “the smallest instance that a recursive method answers directly without calling itself” describes which of the following?
o: Recursion
Divide and conquer
Binary search
Base case
items.s: Base case is the smallest instance that a recursive method answers directly without calling itself.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: Which term is described by “a method that repeatedly picks the smallest remaining item and puts it in its final place”?
o: Counting sort
Merge sort
Bubble sort
Selection sort
items.s: Selection sort is a method that repeatedly picks the smallest remaining item and puts it in its final place.

items.q: Which term is described by “a link that may be travelled one way only”?
o: Directed edge
Single component network
Depth first search
Covering subgraph
items.s: Directed edge is a link that may be travelled one way only.

items.q: Quick sort may be defined as
o: a divide and conquer method that partitions about a chosen item and then sorts the parts
an upper limit on growth, stating that a function never rises faster than another beyond some size
the bunching of occupied positions that makes later probes longer
the splitting of a problem into parts, the solving of each, and the joining of the results
items.s: Quick sort: a divide and conquer method that partitions about a chosen item and then sorts the parts. The other options describe Clustering, Big O notation, Divide and conquer.

items.q: Covering subgraph may be defined as
o: the single node at the top of a tree from which every other node is reached
a tree that touches every point of a graph using only links that the graph already has
an upper limit on growth, stating that a function never rises faster than another beyond some size
a graph in which a path exists between every pair of points
items.s: Covering subgraph: a tree that touches every point of a graph using only links that the graph already has. The other options describe Root, Big O notation, Single component network.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Linked list?
o: a chain of separately stored nodes in which each node names the one that follows it
a structure in which each entry names both the neighbour before it and the neighbour after it
the repeated exchange of an item with its better child until the ordering rule holds again
an equation that expresses the cost of a method in terms of the cost of smaller inputs
items.s: Linked list: a chain of separately stored nodes in which each node names the one that follows it. The other options describe Two way linkage, Recurrence relation, Sift down.

items.q: Which term is described by “the abandoning of a partial attempt as soon as it cannot be completed and the trying of another”?
o: Dynamic programming
Binary search
Backtracking
Base case
items.s: Backtracking is the abandoning of a partial attempt as soon as it cannot be completed and the trying of another.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: Which of the following best describes Weighted edge?
o: a container that always hands back the item of highest rank rather than the earliest or latest
a statement of how much extra storage a method needs as the size of the input grows
a link that carries a number standing for cost, distance or time
a sorting method that repeatedly takes away the best item of a ranked tree and refills the gap
items.s: Weighted edge: a link that carries a number standing for cost, distance or time. The other options describe Repeated top removal sort, Space complexity, Priority queue.

items.q: The statement “the single node at the top of a tree from which every other node is reached” describes which of the following?
o: Height of a tree
Postorder traversal
Root
Preorder traversal
items.s: Root is the single node at the top of a tree from which every other node is reached.

items.q: The statement “the largest amount of work the method can be forced to do on any input of a given size” describes which of the following?
o: In place method
Cost growth
Worst case cost
Big O notation
items.s: Worst case cost is the largest amount of work the method can be forced to do on any input of a given size.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: Hard case may be defined as
o: the case in which two different keys are sent to the same position
the checking of items one after another until the wanted one is found or the list ends
the storing of a complete tree in consecutive cells so that a child is found by arithmetic on its parent index
a task for which no method with polynomial running time is known
items.s: Hard case: a task for which no method with polynomial running time is known. The other options describe Linear search, Collision, Implicit layout.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Selection sort?
o: the number of edges on the longest path from the top node down to a leaf
the repeated exchange of a new item with its parent until the ordering rule holds again
a method that repeatedly picks the smallest remaining item and puts it in its final place
the abandoning of a partial attempt as soon as it cannot be completed and the trying of another
items.s: Selection sort: a method that repeatedly picks the smallest remaining item and puts it in its final place. The other options describe Height of a tree, Sift up, Backtracking.

items.q: Which term is described by “an exchange method that repeatedly swaps neighbours that are out of order”?
o: Merge sort
Bubble sort
Counting sort
Comparison sort
items.s: Bubble sort is an exchange method that repeatedly swaps neighbours that are out of order.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Dynamic structure.
o: a container that grows and shrinks while the program runs
a link that carries a number standing for cost, distance or time
the storing of a complete tree in consecutive cells so that a child is found by arithmetic on its parent index
the handling of a clash by keeping a chain of items at each position
items.s: Dynamic structure: a container that grows and shrinks while the program runs. The other options describe Implicit layout, Chaining, Weighted edge.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Leaf.
o: a node that has no children at all
the number of stored items divided by the number of positions available
the storing of a complete tree in consecutive cells so that a child is found by arithmetic on its parent index
the single node at the top of a tree from which every other node is reached
items.s: Leaf: a node that has no children at all. The other options describe Load factor, Root, Implicit layout.

items.q: Which term is described by “the single node at the top of a tree from which every other node is reached”?
o: Root
Inorder traversal
Branching count
Height of a tree
items.s: Root is the single node at the top of a tree from which every other node is reached.

items.q: The statement “the condition reached when an attempt is made to remove from a container that holds nothing” describes which of the following?
o: Underflow
Overflow
Circular buffer
Priority queue
items.s: Underflow is the condition reached when an attempt is made to remove from a container that holds nothing.

items.q: Which term is described by “the condition reached when an attempt is made to remove from a container that holds nothing”?
o: Call stack
Underflow
Queue
Overflow
items.s: Underflow is the condition reached when an attempt is made to remove from a container that holds nothing.

items.q: The statement “the number of edges on the longest path from the top node down to a leaf” describes which of the following?
o: Height of a tree
Leaf
Level
Branching count
items.s: Height of a tree is the number of edges on the longest path from the top node down to a leaf.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Recurrence relation?
o: an equation that expresses the cost of a method in terms of the cost of smaller inputs
the work expected when all inputs of a given size are taken as equally likely
the searching for a free position by stepping forward one place at a time
the single node at the top of a tree from which every other node is reached
items.s: Recurrence relation: an equation that expresses the cost of a method in terms of the cost of smaller inputs. The other options describe Average case cost, Root, Linear probing.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Counting sort?
o: the family of problems whose yes answers can be checked quickly when a guess is supplied
a method that orders items by tallying how many times each key value occurs
a chain of separately stored nodes in which each node names the one that follows it
the largest amount of work the method can be forced to do on any input of a given size
items.s: Counting sort: a method that orders items by tallying how many times each key value occurs. The other options describe Linked list, Nondeterministic class, Worst case cost.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Recurrence relation?
o: the storage of a graph as one chain of neighbours for each point
the act of placing a new item on top of a collection that only grows at one end
the repeated exchange of a new item with its parent until the ordering rule holds again
an equation that expresses the cost of a method in terms of the cost of smaller inputs
items.s: Recurrence relation: an equation that expresses the cost of a method in terms of the cost of smaller inputs. The other options describe Sift up, Push, Adjacency list.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Graph?
o: a method that learns the order of the items only by comparing pairs
the exploration of a graph by visiting all neighbours of a point before going deeper
the exploration of a graph by following one route as far as possible before backing up
a set of points together with a set of pairs showing which points are joined
items.s: Graph: a set of points together with a set of pairs showing which points are joined. The other options describe Comparison sort, Depth first search, Breadth first search.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Circular buffer.
o: the saving of answers to overlapping smaller problems so that none is worked out twice
a fixed block of cells used as a queue by letting the rear index wrap round to the start
the reference that names the first node of a chain and from which the rest are reached
an upper limit on growth, stating that a function never rises faster than another beyond some size
items.s: Circular buffer: a fixed block of cells used as a queue by letting the rear index wrap round to the start. The other options describe Dynamic programming, Head pointer, Big O notation.

items.q: The statement “the distance of a node from the top, counted in edges” describes which of the following?
o: Level
Branching count
Ordered lookup tree
Binary tree
items.s: Level is the distance of a node from the top, counted in edges.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Postorder traversal.
o: a container that always hands back the item of highest rank rather than the earliest or latest
the visiting of both subtrees of a node before the node itself
the checking of items one after another until the wanted one is found or the list ends
a structure in which each entry names both the neighbour before it and the neighbour after it
items.s: Postorder traversal: the visiting of both subtrees of a node before the node itself. The other options describe Two way linkage, Priority queue, Linear search.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Chaining?
o: the handling of a clash by keeping a chain of items at each position
a container in which the item most recently put in is the first one taken out
the repeated exchange of a new item with its parent until the ordering rule holds again
a structure in which each entry names both the neighbour before it and the neighbour after it
items.s: Chaining: the handling of a clash by keeping a chain of items at each position. The other options describe Sift up, Stack, Two way linkage.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Load factor.
o: the rebuilding of a table in a larger space with a new rule when it becomes too full
a set of points together with a set of pairs showing which points are joined
the number of stored items divided by the number of positions available
the visiting of every item of a structure once in a stated order
items.s: Load factor: the number of stored items divided by the number of positions available. The other options describe Graph, Rehashing, Traversal.

items.q: Which term is described by “the condition reached when an attempt is made to add to a container that is already full”?
o: Pop
Overflow
Priority queue
Underflow
items.s: Overflow is the condition reached when an attempt is made to add to a container that is already full.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Node?
o: a finite sequence of unambiguous steps that turns an input into the required output and then stops
one unit of a linked structure that carries an item and the link or links to its neighbours
the handling of a clash by keeping a chain of items at each position
the work expected when all inputs of a given size are taken as equally likely
items.s: Node: one unit of a linked structure that carries an item and the link or links to its neighbours. The other options describe Chaining, Average case cost, Algorithm.

items.q: Which of the following best describes In place method?
o: a procedure that rearranges its input using only a fixed amount of extra storage
a method that solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version of the same problem
a task for which no method with polynomial running time is known
a procedure that makes its choices with the help of a random source
items.s: In place method: a procedure that rearranges its input using only a fixed amount of extra storage. The other options describe Recursion, Hard case, Randomised method.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Repeated top removal sort.
o: the number of edges on the longest path from the top node down to a leaf
a tree that touches every point of a graph using only links that the graph already has
a dummy entry placed at the boundary of a chain to remove special cases from the code
a sorting method that repeatedly takes away the best item of a ranked tree and refills the gap
items.s: Repeated top removal sort: a sorting method that repeatedly takes away the best item of a ranked tree and refills the gap. The other options describe Height of a tree, Guard cell, Covering subgraph.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Covering subgraph?
o: a container in which the item most recently put in is the first one taken out
a tree that touches every point of a graph using only links that the graph already has
a task for which no method with polynomial running time is known
the checking of items one after another until the wanted one is found or the list ends
items.s: Covering subgraph: a tree that touches every point of a graph using only links that the graph already has. The other options describe Stack, Hard case, Linear search.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Level?
o: a chain of separately stored nodes in which each node names the one that follows it
the number of children that hang directly below a given entry
a structure in which each entry names both the neighbour before it and the neighbour after it
the distance of a node from the top, counted in edges
items.s: Level: the distance of a node from the top, counted in edges. The other options describe Linked list, Two way linkage, Branching count.

items.q: Sift down may be defined as
o: the abandoning of a partial attempt as soon as it cannot be completed and the trying of another
the number of children that hang directly below a given entry
the repeated exchange of an item with its better child until the ordering rule holds again
a task for which a method with polynomial running time is known
items.s: Sift down: the repeated exchange of an item with its better child until the ordering rule holds again. The other options describe Branching count, Polynomially solvable case, Backtracking.

items.q: Which term is described by “a method that orders items by tallying how many times each key value occurs”?
o: Bubble sort
Comparison sort
Radix sort
Counting sort
items.s: Counting sort is a method that orders items by tallying how many times each key value occurs.

items.q: Which term is described by “a method that learns the order of the items only by comparing pairs”?
o: Merge sort
Selection sort
Quick sort
Comparison sort
items.s: Comparison sort is a method that learns the order of the items only by comparing pairs.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Nondeterministic class?
o: a method that grows a sorted front part by sliding each new item into its place
a dummy entry placed at the boundary of a chain to remove special cases from the code
the family of problems whose yes answers can be checked quickly when a guess is supplied
the showing that one problem can be solved by a method for another
items.s: Nondeterministic class: the family of problems whose yes answers can be checked quickly when a guess is supplied. The other options describe Reduction, Guard cell, Insertion sort.

items.q: Which term is described by “a statement of how much extra storage a method needs as the size of the input grows”?
o: Big O notation
Big theta notation
Space complexity
Worst case cost
items.s: Space complexity is a statement of how much extra storage a method needs as the size of the input grows.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Hash table?
o: a statement of how much extra storage a method needs as the size of the input grows
a block of positions into which items are placed by a computed index
a method that orders items by processing their digit positions one at a time
a structure in which each entry names both the neighbour before it and the neighbour after it
items.s: Hash table: a block of positions into which items are placed by a computed index. The other options describe Space complexity, Radix sort, Two way linkage.

items.q: Average case cost may be defined as
o: the handling of a clash by looking for another free position in the same table
the work expected when all inputs of a given size are taken as equally likely
the storage of a graph as one chain of neighbours for each point
the smallest instance that a recursive method answers directly without calling itself
items.s: Average case cost: the work expected when all inputs of a given size are taken as equally likely. The other options describe Base case, Adjacency list, Open addressing.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: Which of the following best describes Dynamic programming?
o: the rebuilding of a table in a larger space with a new rule when it becomes too full
the saving of answers to overlapping smaller problems so that none is worked out twice
a divide and conquer method that sorts two halves and then interleaves them
the largest amount of work the method can be forced to do on any input of a given size
items.s: Dynamic programming: the saving of answers to overlapping smaller problems so that none is worked out twice. The other options describe Rehashing, Worst case cost, Merge sort.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: The statement “an equation that expresses the cost of a method in terms of the cost of smaller inputs” describes which of the following?
o: Recurrence relation
Backtracking
Recursion
Binary search
items.s: Recurrence relation is an equation that expresses the cost of a method in terms of the cost of smaller inputs.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Dynamic structure?
o: a sorting method that repeatedly takes away the best item of a ranked tree and refills the gap
the repeated exchange of a new item with its parent until the ordering rule holds again
a container that grows and shrinks while the program runs
the smallest instance that a recursive method answers directly without calling itself
items.s: Dynamic structure: a container that grows and shrinks while the program runs. The other options describe Base case, Repeated top removal sort, Sift up.

items.q: Sift up may be defined as
o: the checking of items one after another until the wanted one is found or the list ends
the exploration of a graph by visiting all neighbours of a point before going deeper
an equation that expresses the cost of a method in terms of the cost of smaller inputs
the repeated exchange of a new item with its parent until the ordering rule holds again
items.s: Sift up: the repeated exchange of a new item with its parent until the ordering rule holds again. The other options describe Linear search, Breadth first search, Recurrence relation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Postorder traversal?
o: the item about which a partition is arranged
a square table whose entry shows whether a pair of points is joined
the visiting of both subtrees of a node before the node itself
the largest amount of work the method can be forced to do on any input of a given size
items.s: Postorder traversal: the visiting of both subtrees of a node before the node itself. The other options describe Adjacency matrix, Pivot, Worst case cost.

items.q: Linear search may be defined as
o: a rule that turns a key into a position number in a table
the visiting of a node before either of its subtrees
a container in which the item put in earliest is the first one taken out
the checking of items one after another until the wanted one is found or the list ends
items.s: Linear search: the checking of items one after another until the wanted one is found or the list ends. The other options describe Hash function, Preorder traversal, Queue.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Postorder traversal?
o: a method that orders items by tallying how many times each key value occurs
the visiting of both subtrees of a node before the node itself
a tree that touches every point of a graph using only links that the graph already has
a block of positions into which items are placed by a computed index
items.s: Postorder traversal: the visiting of both subtrees of a node before the node itself. The other options describe Hash table, Counting sort, Covering subgraph.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Call stack?
o: a method that grows a sorted front part by sliding each new item into its place
the exploration of a graph by visiting all neighbours of a point before going deeper
a block of positions into which items are placed by a computed index
the record of nested routine activations that grows as calls begin and shrinks as they return
items.s: Call stack: the record of nested routine activations that grows as calls begin and shrinks as they return. The other options describe Insertion sort, Hash table, Breadth first search.

items.q: The statement “the bunching of occupied positions that makes later probes longer” describes which of the following?
o: Open addressing
Collision
Chaining
Clustering
items.s: Clustering is the bunching of occupied positions that makes later probes longer.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Collision.
o: the case in which two different keys are sent to the same position
the exploration of a graph by visiting all neighbours of a point before going deeper
a sorting method that repeatedly takes away the best item of a ranked tree and refills the gap
the forming of a heap from an unordered block by repairing the lower nodes first
items.s: Collision: the case in which two different keys are sent to the same position. The other options describe Breadth first search, Heapify, Repeated top removal sort.

items.q: The naive method for multiplying two 10 by 10 matrices performs two operations for every triple of indices. How many operations does it perform?
items.s: There are n cubed = 1000 triples and two operations for each, so 2000 operations.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A loop considers every unordered pair of distinct items drawn from an input of size 32, taking each pair once. How many pairs are examined?
items.s: The pairs number n(n-1)/2, that is 32 x 31 / 2 = 496.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A two dimensional array with 5 rows and 14 columns of 8 byte elements is stored row by row starting at address 1000. What is the address of the element in row 0 and column 1?
items.s: Its position in the block is row x columns + column = 1, so the address is 1000 + 1 x 8 = 1008.

items.q: A singly linked chain holds 2000 nodes, each carrying a 4 byte item and a pointer of 4 bytes. How many bytes of storage does the chain occupy?
items.s: Each node takes 4 + 4 = 8 bytes, so 2000 nodes take 16000 bytes.

items.q: A chain of 5000 nodes is walked from the head to the node in position 250, counting the head as position one. How many nodes are passed through?
items.s: The walk stops at position 250 having passed through exactly 250 nodes.

items.q: A circular queue uses 32 cells and its rear index currently stands at 1. After 3 further insertions, which index holds the rear?
items.s: Each insertion advances the index by one and wraps at 32, so (1 + 3) mod 32 = 4.

items.q: A binary tree has every level filled to the bottom, where the height is 5 and the root sits at level one. How many leaves does it have?
items.s: The bottom level is level 5 and carries 2^4 = 16 nodes, all of them leaves.

items.q: In a full binary tree numbered with the root at level one, how many nodes stand on level 6?
items.s: Level one has one node and every level doubles the count, so level 6 holds 2^5 = 32 nodes.

items.q: A binary heap is stored in an array with the root at index 0. What is the index of the parent of the node at index 54?
items.s: The parent of index i sits at (i - 1)/2 rounded down, so (54 - 1)/2 = 26.

items.q: A binary heap is stored in an array with the root at index 0. What is the index of the right child of the node at index 10?
items.s: The left child sits at 2i + 1 and the right at 2i + 2, so 2 x 10 + 2 = 22.

items.q: A hash table has 250 positions and holds 45 keys. Calculate its load factor.
items.s: The load factor is keys divided by positions: 45/250 = 0.18.

items.q: A hash table with 60 positions uses chaining and holds 100 keys. Taking the keys as evenly spread as possible, what is the average chain length?
items.s: The keys are shared among 60 positions, so each chain holds 100/60 = 1.67 keys on average.

items.q: A directed graph has 10 vertices and at most one arrow from any vertex to any other. What is the largest number of arrows it can have?
items.s: Each of the 10 vertices may point at each of the other 9, so there can be 90 arrows.

items.q: The adjacency matrix of a graph with 500 vertices is stored with 1 byte per entry. How many bytes does the matrix occupy?
items.s: The matrix has 500 x 500 = 250000 entries, which take 250000 bytes.

items.q: A spanning tree is to be formed for a connected graph with 500 vertices. How many edges does the tree contain?
items.s: A tree on 500 vertices always has one edge fewer than vertices, that is 499.

items.q: Insertion sort is applied to an array of 50 items arranged in decreasing order. How many shifts of elements are carried out?
items.s: The worst case shifts 1 + 2 + ... + (50 - 1) elements, which is n(n-1)/2 = 1225.

items.q: A radix sort processes 200 keys and each key is examined once for each of its 2 digits. How many key examinations does the method make?
items.s: Every pass looks at all 200 keys, and there are 2 passes, so 400 examinations are made.

items.q: A linear search is made for a key that is absent from an array of 10000 items. How many comparisons are needed before the search can report failure?
items.s: Every item is compared before the search can stop, so 10000 comparisons are made.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: A table of the smallest numbers of coins for every amount up to 10 is filled one amount at a time. How many entries are filled?
items.s: The amounts from one to 10 each take one entry, so 10 entries are filled.

items.q: An algorithm halves its input at every step. How many steps does it need for an input of size 65536?
items.s: The number of halvings satisfies 2^k = 65536, so k = 16 steps.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A method performs 8 basic operations for each item of an input of size 5000. How many operations does it carry out in all?
items.s: The work is 8 operations per item times 5000 items, that is 40000 operations.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A divide and conquer method splits an input of size 1024 into halves, spends 3 operations on every item at each level and has 10 levels in all. How many operations does it perform?
items.s: One level costs 3 x 1024 = 3072 operations and there are 10 levels, giving 30720 operations.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A method needs one 8 byte record for each of the 1000 items of its input. How much storage does the working copy occupy, in bytes?
items.s: The copy holds 1000 records of 8 bytes, that is 8000 bytes.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: An array of 16 byte elements begins at address 16384. What is the address of the element with index 22?
items.s: The address is base + index x element size = 16384 + 22 x 16 = 16736.

items.q: A doubly linked chain holds 200 nodes, each carrying a 32 byte item and two pointers of 4 bytes. How many bytes of storage does the chain occupy?
items.s: Each node takes 32 + 8 = 40 bytes, so the whole chain takes 8000 bytes.

items.q: An item is to be inserted into a sorted array of 100 elements at index 86. How many existing elements must be moved one place to the right?
items.s: Every element from index 86 onwards shifts, which is 100 - 86 = 14 elements.

items.q: A simulation performs 200 operations; 80 per cent of them push and the rest pop. How many pushes occur?
items.s: The pushes are 80/100 x 200 = 160 operations.

items.q: A stack is held in a block of 2000 bytes and each item occupies 2 bytes. How many items can it hold?
items.s: The block holds 2000/2 = 1000 items.

items.q: The postfix expression 2 8 * is evaluated with a stack. What result is left on the stack?
items.s: The two values are pushed and the operator * combines them, giving 2 * 8 = 16.

items.q: A complete binary tree holds 255 nodes. What is its height, counted as the number of edges on the longest path from the root?
items.s: A complete tree of 255 nodes has floor(log2(255)) = 7 edges on its longest path.

items.q: A full binary tree holds 127 nodes in all. How many of them are internal, that is not leaves?
items.s: A full binary tree of n nodes has (n - 1)/2 internal nodes, so (127 - 1)/2 = 63.

items.q: Keys are inserted into an empty binary search tree in strict increasing order. How many edges are on the longest path from the root when 31 keys have been inserted?
items.s: Every key becomes the right child of the one before it, so the tree is a chain with 31 - 1 = 30 edges.

items.q: An inorder traversal of a binary search tree holding 15 nodes stops as soon as it has visited 2 nodes. How many nodes remain unvisited?
items.s: The traversal has visited 2 of the 15 nodes, so 13 of them are still unvisited.

items.q: A balanced binary search tree holds 31 keys. What is the greatest number of nodes examined by one lookup?
items.s: The search follows one node per level, and a balanced tree of 31 keys has 5 levels.

items.q: A heap holds 511 items in an array. What is the height of the tree it forms, counted in edges?
items.s: The tree is complete, so its height is the floor of log2 of the count: floor(log2(511)) = 8.

items.q: A heap is built by repairing every internal node of a complete tree holding 255 items, from the lowest upwards. How many nodes are repaired?
items.s: The leaves need no repair, and a complete tree of 255 items has 128 of them, leaving 127 internal nodes.

items.q: Heap sort is applied to 256 items. Taking each removal as costing at most 8 sift steps, what is the largest total number of sift steps?
items.s: Each of the 256 removals costs at most 8 steps, so the total is at most 2048.

items.q: Keys are placed in a table of 23 positions by taking the remainder of the key on division by 23. At which position does the key 512 land?
items.s: The remainder of 512 on division by 23 is 6.

items.q: A table of 40 positions uses linear probing. The positions from 15 through 19 are already occupied and the one after them is free. A key whose home position is 15 is inserted. How many probes does it take?
items.s: The occupied run holds 5 positions, so the key probes those 5 and then the free one, taking 6 probes in all.

items.q: A table holds 50 keys and the load factor must not exceed 50 per cent. What is the smallest number of positions that will serve?
items.s: The positions needed satisfy keys/positions at most 50/100, so at least 50 x 100/50 = 100 positions are required.

items.q: A chained hash table holds 100 keys, each key takes 12 bytes and each chain pointer takes 8 bytes. How many bytes do the key records occupy in all?
items.s: Each record takes 12 + 8 = 20 bytes, so 100 records take 2000 bytes.

items.q: An undirected graph has 15 vertices and no two are joined by more than one edge. What is the largest number of edges it can have?
items.s: Every vertex can reach the other n - 1, so the edges number 15 x 14 / 2 = 105.

items.q: An undirected graph with 50 vertices and 100 edges is stored as adjacency lists, each link taking 4 bytes and each list header taking 4 bytes. How many bytes are needed?
items.s: There are 50 headers and 2 x 100 = 200 links, so the total is 200 + 800 = 1000 bytes.

items.q: A breadth first search starts at a vertex that has 4 neighbours, and every later vertex also has 4 neighbours. How many vertices stand on level 2 of the search?
items.s: The front grows by the factor 4 - 1 at each step, so level 2 holds 4 x 3^1 = 12 vertices.

items.q: A graph has 12 vertices and every vertex has degree 5. How many edges does the graph contain?
items.s: The degrees total 12 x 5 = 60, and each edge is counted twice, so there are 30 edges.

items.q: Bubble sort is applied to an array of 20 items that happens to be in reverse order, so no pass ends early. How many comparisons are made?
items.s: The passes compare 20 - 1, then 20 - 2 and so on, which adds to n(n-1)/2 = 190.

items.q: Merge sort is applied to 256 items. Into how many levels of splitting does the recursion divide the work?
items.s: The array is halved until single items remain, which takes log2(256) = 8 levels.

items.q: Merge sort is applied to 16 items and every level of the recursion does at most 16 comparisons in all. What is the largest total number of comparisons?
items.s: Each of the 4 levels costs at most 16 comparisons, so the total is at most 64.

items.q: A partition about a pivot leaves 3 items to the left of the pivot and 46 to its right in an array of 50 items. The right part is then sorted by a method that compares every pair once. How many comparisons does that part need?
items.s: The right part holds 46 items, so its pair comparisons number m(m-1)/2 = 1035.

items.q: Binary search is applied to a sorted array of 63 items. What is the greatest number of comparisons it can make?
items.s: Each comparison halves the range, and the least k with 2^k at least 63 + 1 is 6.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: A linear search is made for a key that is known to be present in an array of 2000 items and every position is equally likely. What is the average number of comparisons?
items.s: The positions need 1 up to 2000 comparisons with equal chance, so the average is (2000 + 1)/2 = 1000.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: A recursive method makes 3 calls from every activation and the recursion has depth 3. Counting the first call as level zero, how many activations are created in all?
items.s: The levels hold 1, 3, 3 squared and so on up to 3^3, which adds to 40 activations.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: The unmodified recursive method for the 20th Fibonacci number makes one call for each node of its recursion tree. How many calls does it make in all?
items.s: The tree has 2 x F(21) - 1 nodes, and F(21) = 10946, so the calls number 21891.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: A recurrence splits an input of size 64 into 4 equal parts and costs nothing outside the recursive calls. How many levels does the tree of calls have?
items.s: The size falls from 64 to one by dividing by 4, which needs log_4(64) = 3 levels.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: A dynamic programming method for choosing items keeps one row for the empty choice and one row for each of 5 items, and one column for zero capacity and one for each of 10 capacity units. How many cells does the table hold?
items.s: The table has 5 + 1 = 6 rows and 10 + 1 = 11 columns, so it holds 66 cells.

items.q: A file of 2000 items is sorted at a cost of n log2 n comparisons and then searched 50 times by binary search. Taking log2 2000 as 10 and the cost of one binary search as 11 comparisons, how many comparisons are made in all?
items.s: The sort costs 2000 x 10 = 20000 comparisons and the searches cost 50 x 11 = 550, giving 20550 in all.

items.q: A nested loop runs an inner block whose cost is 4 operations once for every ordered pair of items in an input of size 100. How many operations are carried out?
items.s: There are n squared = 10000 ordered pairs, each costing 4, so the total is 40000.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A loop considers every unordered pair of distinct items drawn from an input of size 20, taking each pair once. How many pairs are examined?
items.s: The pairs number n(n-1)/2, that is 20 x 19 / 2 = 190.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A two dimensional array with 21 rows and 13 columns of 4 byte elements is stored row by row starting at address 4000. What is the address of the element in row 19 and column 10?
items.s: Its position in the block is row x columns + column = 257, so the address is 4000 + 257 x 4 = 5028.

items.q: A circular queue uses 32 cells and its rear index currently stands at 31. After 3 further insertions, which index holds the rear?
items.s: Each insertion advances the index by one and wraps at 32, so (31 + 3) mod 32 = 2.

items.q: The statement “a block of consecutive cells holding items of the same kind, reached by position number” describes which of the following?
o: Traversal
Head pointer
Dynamic structure
Array
items.s: Array is a block of consecutive cells holding items of the same kind, reached by position number.

items.q: The best definition of Postorder traversal among these is
o: the visiting of a node before either of its subtrees
a hierarchy in which every key is larger than all keys to its left and smaller than all to its right
the visiting of a left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree
the visiting of both subtrees of a node before the node itself
items.s: Postorder traversal: the visiting of both subtrees of a node before the node itself. The other options describe Preorder traversal, Ordered lookup tree, Inorder traversal.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Radix sort means.
o: a divide and conquer method that partitions about a chosen item and then sorts the parts
a method that orders items by processing their digit positions one at a time
a method that repeatedly picks the smallest remaining item and puts it in its final place
an exchange method that repeatedly swaps neighbours that are out of order
items.s: Radix sort: a method that orders items by processing their digit positions one at a time. The other options describe Bubble sort, Selection sort, Quick sort.

items.q: In this course, Space complexity refers to
o: a statement of how much extra storage a method needs as the size of the input grows
a finite sequence of unambiguous steps that turns an input into the required output and then stops
an upper limit on growth, stating that a function never rises faster than another beyond some size
a two sided limit showing that two functions grow at the same rate up to constant factors
items.s: Space complexity: a statement of how much extra storage a method needs as the size of the input grows. The other options describe Big theta notation, Algorithm, Big O notation.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: Randomised method is best described as
o: the showing that one problem can be solved by a method for another
a procedure that makes its choices with the help of a random source
a procedure that gives a good but not always best answer within a stated bound
a task for which no method with polynomial running time is known
items.s: Randomised method: a procedure that makes its choices with the help of a random source. The other options describe Approximation method, Reduction, Hard case.

items.q: The best definition of Height of a tree among these is
o: a structure in which every node has at most a left child and a right child
the number of children that hang directly below a given entry
the visiting of a node before either of its subtrees
the number of edges on the longest path from the top node down to a leaf
items.s: Height of a tree: the number of edges on the longest path from the top node down to a leaf. The other options describe Binary tree, Preorder traversal, Branching count.

items.q: The best definition of Worst case cost among these is
o: a procedure that rearranges its input using only a fixed amount of extra storage
the largest amount of work the method can be forced to do on any input of a given size
a statement of how much extra storage a method needs as the size of the input grows
an upper limit on growth, stating that a function never rises faster than another beyond some size
items.s: Worst case cost: the largest amount of work the method can be forced to do on any input of a given size. The other options describe Big O notation, In place method, Space complexity.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Two way linkage means.
o: one unit of a linked structure that carries an item and the link or links to its neighbours
a block of consecutive cells holding items of the same kind, reached by position number
a structure in which each entry names both the neighbour before it and the neighbour after it
a dummy entry placed at the boundary of a chain to remove special cases from the code
items.s: Two way linkage: a structure in which each entry names both the neighbour before it and the neighbour after it. The other options describe Array, Guard cell, Node.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Collision means.
o: the handling of a clash by keeping a chain of items at each position
a block of positions into which items are placed by a computed index
the case in which two different keys are sent to the same position
the number of stored items divided by the number of positions available
items.s: Collision: the case in which two different keys are sent to the same position. The other options describe Load factor, Hash table, Chaining.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a question whose answer is simply yes or no”
o: Polynomially solvable case
Nondeterministic class
Approximation method
Decision problem
items.s: Decision problem is a question whose answer is simply yes or no.

items.q: Big omega notation is best described as
o: a finite sequence of unambiguous steps that turns an input into the required output and then stops
the work expected when all inputs of a given size are taken as equally likely

items.q: A doubly linked chain holds 100 nodes, each carrying a 4 byte item and two pointers of 4 bytes. How many bytes of storage does the chain occupy?
items.s: Each node takes 4 + 8 = 12 bytes, so the whole chain takes 1200 bytes.

items.q: An item is to be inserted into a sorted array of 500 elements at index 150. How many existing elements must be moved one place to the right?
items.s: Every element from index 150 onwards shifts, which is 500 - 150 = 350 elements.

items.q: The postfix expression 7 7 - is evaluated with a stack. What result is left on the stack?
items.s: The two values are pushed and the operator - combines them, giving 7 - 7 = 0.

items.q: A complete binary tree holds 63 nodes. What is its height, counted as the number of edges on the longest path from the root?
items.s: A complete tree of 63 nodes has floor(log2(63)) = 5 edges on its longest path.

items.q: A full binary tree holds 31 nodes in all. How many of them are internal, that is not leaves?
items.s: A full binary tree of n nodes has (n - 1)/2 internal nodes, so (31 - 1)/2 = 15.

items.q: A heap holds 255 items in an array. What is the height of the tree it forms, counted in edges?
items.s: The tree is complete, so its height is the floor of log2 of the count: floor(log2(255)) = 7.

items.q: An item is sifted up from the bottom of a complete heap holding 512 items. What is the greatest number of exchanges it can take part in?
items.s: One exchange is possible per level and the tree has floor(log2(512)) = 9 levels above the bottom.

items.q: A table holds 200 keys and the load factor must not exceed 80 per cent. What is the smallest number of positions that will serve?
items.s: The positions needed satisfy keys/positions at most 80/100, so at least 200 x 100/80 = 250 positions are required.

items.q: A chained hash table holds 500 keys, each key takes 12 bytes and each chain pointer takes 4 bytes. How many bytes do the key records occupy in all?
items.s: Each record takes 12 + 4 = 16 bytes, so 500 records take 8000 bytes.

items.q: An undirected graph with 200 vertices and 1000 edges is stored as adjacency lists, each link taking 8 bytes and each list header taking 8 bytes. How many bytes are needed?
items.s: There are 200 headers and 2 x 1000 = 2000 links, so the total is 1600 + 16000 = 17600 bytes.

items.q: A graph has 8 vertices and every vertex has degree 5. How many edges does the graph contain?
items.s: The degrees total 8 x 5 = 40, and each edge is counted twice, so there are 20 edges.

items.q: Merge sort is applied to 32 items. Into how many levels of splitting does the recursion divide the work?
items.s: The array is halved until single items remain, which takes log2(32) = 5 levels.

items.q: A recursive method makes 4 calls from every activation and the recursion has depth 4. Counting the first call as level zero, how many activations are created in all?
items.s: The levels hold 1, 4, 4 squared and so on up to 4^4, which adds to 341 activations.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: A recurrence splits an input of size 16 into 4 equal parts and costs nothing outside the recursive calls. How many levels does the tree of calls have?
items.s: The size falls from 16 to one by dividing by 4, which needs log_4(16) = 2 levels.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: A dynamic programming method for choosing items keeps one row for the empty choice and one row for each of 8 items, and one column for zero capacity and one for each of 8 capacity units. How many cells does the table hold?
items.s: The table has 8 + 1 = 9 rows and 8 + 1 = 9 columns, so it holds 81 cells.

items.q: An algorithm halves its input at every step. How many steps does it need for an input of size 4096?
items.s: The number of halvings satisfies 2^k = 4096, so k = 12 steps.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A method performs 10 basic operations for each item of an input of size 250. How many operations does it carry out in all?
items.s: The work is 10 operations per item times 250 items, that is 2500 operations.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A nested loop runs an inner block whose cost is 1 operations once for every ordered pair of items in an input of size 40. How many operations are carried out?
items.s: There are n squared = 1600 ordered pairs, each costing 1, so the total is 1600.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: The naive method for multiplying two 50 by 50 matrices performs two operations for every triple of indices. How many operations does it perform?
items.s: There are n cubed = 125000 triples and two operations for each, so 250000 operations.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A loop considers every unordered pair of distinct items drawn from an input of size 12, taking each pair once. How many pairs are examined?
items.s: The pairs number n(n-1)/2, that is 12 x 11 / 2 = 66.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A method needs one 2 byte record for each of the 2000 items of its input. How much storage does the working copy occupy, in bytes?
items.s: The copy holds 2000 records of 2 bytes, that is 4000 bytes.

items.q: An array of 8 byte elements begins at address 8000. What is the address of the element with index 51?
items.s: The address is base + index x element size = 8000 + 51 x 8 = 8408.

items.q: A two dimensional array with 18 rows and 26 columns of 2 byte elements is stored row by row starting at address 0. What is the address of the element in row 13 and column 6?
items.s: Its position in the block is row x columns + column = 344, so the address is 0 + 344 x 2 = 688.

items.q: A singly linked chain holds 250 nodes, each carrying a 12 byte item and a pointer of 4 bytes. How many bytes of storage does the chain occupy?
items.s: Each node takes 12 + 4 = 16 bytes, so 250 nodes take 4000 bytes.

items.q: A chain of 10000 nodes is walked from the head to the node in position 250, counting the head as position one. How many nodes are passed through?
items.s: The walk stops at position 250 having passed through exactly 250 nodes.

items.q: A simulation performs 200 operations; 60 per cent of them push and the rest pop. How many pushes occur?
items.s: The pushes are 60/100 x 200 = 120 operations.

items.q: A circular queue uses 32 cells and its rear index currently stands at 31. After 2 further insertions, which index holds the rear?
items.s: Each insertion advances the index by one and wraps at 32, so (31 + 2) mod 32 = 1.

items.q: A stack is held in a block of 200 bytes and each item occupies 2 bytes. How many items can it hold?
items.s: The block holds 200/2 = 100 items.

items.q: A balanced expression contains 6 opening brackets and the same number of closing brackets. If every closing bracket causes one pop, how many pop operations occur?
items.s: Each closing bracket matches one opening one, so exactly 6 pops are performed.

items.q: A binary tree of height 8 is as full as it can be at every level. What is the largest number of nodes it can contain, counting the root as level one?
items.s: A full tree of height h holds 2^h - 1 nodes, so 2^8 - 1 = 255.

items.q: A binary tree has every level filled to the bottom, where the height is 6 and the root sits at level one. How many leaves does it have?
items.s: The bottom level is level 6 and carries 2^5 = 32 nodes, all of them leaves.

items.q: An inorder traversal of a binary search tree holding 31 nodes stops as soon as it has visited 2 nodes. How many nodes remain unvisited?
items.s: The traversal has visited 2 of the 31 nodes, so 29 of them are still unvisited.

items.q: A binary heap is stored in an array with the root at index 0. What is the index of the parent of the node at index 100?
items.s: The parent of index i sits at (i - 1)/2 rounded down, so (100 - 1)/2 = 49.

items.q: A binary heap is stored in an array with the root at index 0. What is the index of the right child of the node at index 16?
items.s: The left child sits at 2i + 1 and the right at 2i + 2, so 2 x 16 + 2 = 34.

items.q: A heap is built by repairing every internal node of a complete tree holding 63 items, from the lowest upwards. How many nodes are repaired?
items.s: The leaves need no repair, and a complete tree of 63 items has 32 of them, leaving 31 internal nodes.

items.q: Keys are placed in a table of 29 positions by taking the remainder of the key on division by 29. At which position does the key 1234 land?
items.s: The remainder of 1234 on division by 29 is 16.

items.q: A hash table has 150 positions and holds 45 keys. Calculate its load factor.
items.s: The load factor is keys divided by positions: 45/150 = 0.3.

items.q: A hash table with 20 positions uses chaining and holds 500 keys. Taking the keys as evenly spread as possible, what is the average chain length?
items.s: The keys are shared among 20 positions, so each chain holds 500/20 = 25 keys on average.

items.q: A table of 16 positions uses linear probing. The positions from 0 through 11 are already occupied and the one after them is free. A key whose home position is 0 is inserted. How many probes does it take?
items.s: The occupied run holds 12 positions, so the key probes those 12 and then the free one, taking 13 probes in all.

items.q: A directed graph has 6 vertices and at most one arrow from any vertex to any other. What is the largest number of arrows it can have?
items.s: Each of the 6 vertices may point at each of the other 5, so there can be 30 arrows.

items.q: A breadth first search starts at a vertex that has 8 neighbours, and every later vertex also has 8 neighbours. How many vertices stand on level 2 of the search?
items.s: The front grows by the factor 8 - 1 at each step, so level 2 holds 8 x 7^1 = 56 vertices.

items.q: Bubble sort is applied to an array of 50 items that happens to be in reverse order, so no pass ends early. How many comparisons are made?
items.s: The passes compare 50 - 1, then 50 - 2 and so on, which adds to n(n-1)/2 = 1225.

items.q: Selection sort is applied to an array of 40 items. How many comparisons does it make, whatever the original order?
items.s: The first scan compares 40 items, the next 39, and so on, giving n(n-1)/2 = 780.

items.q: A partition about a pivot leaves 2 items to the left of the pivot and 497 to its right in an array of 500 items. The right part is then sorted by a method that compares every pair once. How many comparisons does that part need?
items.s: The right part holds 497 items, so its pair comparisons number m(m-1)/2 = 123256.

items.q: A radix sort processes 200 keys and each key is examined once for each of its 4 digits. How many key examinations does the method make?
items.s: Every pass looks at all 200 keys, and there are 4 passes, so 800 examinations are made.

items.q: Binary search is applied to a sorted array of 511 items. What is the greatest number of comparisons it can make?
items.s: Each comparison halves the range, and the least k with 2^k at least 511 + 1 is 9.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: A table of the smallest numbers of coins for every amount up to 20 is filled one amount at a time. How many entries are filled?
items.s: The amounts from one to 20 each take one entry, so 20 entries are filled.

items.q: A file of 500 items is sorted at a cost of n log2 n comparisons and then searched 10 times by binary search. Taking log2 500 as 8 and the cost of one binary search as 9 comparisons, how many comparisons are made in all?
items.s: The sort costs 500 x 8 = 4000 comparisons and the searches cost 10 x 9 = 90, giving 4090 in all.

items.q: A divide and conquer method splits an input of size 16 into halves, spends 2 operations on every item at each level and has 4 levels in all. How many operations does it perform?
items.s: One level costs 2 x 16 = 32 operations and there are 4 levels, giving 128 operations.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A doubly linked chain holds 400 nodes, each carrying a 32 byte item and two pointers of 4 bytes. How many bytes of storage does the chain occupy?
items.s: Each node takes 32 + 8 = 40 bytes, so the whole chain takes 16000 bytes.

items.q: An item is to be inserted into a sorted array of 100 elements at index 84. How many existing elements must be moved one place to the right?
items.s: Every element from index 84 onwards shifts, which is 100 - 84 = 16 elements.

items.q: The postfix expression 5 2 - is evaluated with a stack. What result is left on the stack?
items.s: The two values are pushed and the operator - combines them, giving 5 - 2 = 3.

items.q: A complete binary tree holds 127 nodes. What is its height, counted as the number of edges on the longest path from the root?
items.s: A complete tree of 127 nodes has floor(log2(127)) = 6 edges on its longest path.

items.q: A full binary tree holds 255 nodes in all. How many of them are internal, that is not leaves?
items.s: A full binary tree of n nodes has (n - 1)/2 internal nodes, so (255 - 1)/2 = 127.

items.q: A balanced binary search tree holds 63 keys. What is the greatest number of nodes examined by one lookup?
items.s: The search follows one node per level, and a balanced tree of 63 keys has 6 levels.

items.q: A heap holds 15 items in an array. What is the height of the tree it forms, counted in edges?
items.s: The tree is complete, so its height is the floor of log2 of the count: floor(log2(15)) = 3.

items.q: A table holds 75 keys and the load factor must not exceed 80 per cent. What is the smallest number of positions that will serve?
items.s: The positions needed satisfy keys/positions at most 80/100, so at least 75 x 100/80 = 94 positions are required.

items.q: A chained hash table holds 1000 keys, each key takes 12 bytes and each chain pointer takes 4 bytes. How many bytes do the key records occupy in all?
items.s: Each record takes 12 + 4 = 16 bytes, so 1000 records take 16000 bytes.

items.q: An undirected graph with 200 vertices and 100 edges is stored as adjacency lists, each link taking 4 bytes and each list header taking 4 bytes. How many bytes are needed?
items.s: There are 200 headers and 2 x 100 = 200 links, so the total is 800 + 800 = 1600 bytes.

items.q: A graph has 12 vertices and every vertex has degree 3. How many edges does the graph contain?
items.s: The degrees total 12 x 3 = 36, and each edge is counted twice, so there are 18 edges.

a statement of how much extra storage a method needs as the size of the input grows
the work expected when all inputs of a given size are taken as equally likely
a procedure that rearranges its input using only a fixed amount of extra storage
