an equation that expresses the cost of a method in terms of the cost of smaller inputs

items.q: A heap is built by repairing every internal node of a complete tree holding 31 items, from the lowest upwards. How many nodes are repaired?
items.s: The leaves need no repair, and a complete tree of 31 items has 16 of them, leaving 15 internal nodes.

items.q: Heap sort is applied to 512 items. Taking each removal as costing at most 9 sift steps, what is the largest total number of sift steps?
items.s: Each of the 512 removals costs at most 9 steps, so the total is at most 4608.

items.q: The largest item of a list of 1000 items is found by scanning the list once from the second item onwards. How many comparisons are needed?
items.s: The first item is the running largest and each of the other 999 items is compared with it, so 999 comparisons are made.

items.q: A table of 16 positions uses linear probing. The positions from 10 through 10 are already occupied and the one after them is free. A key whose home position is 10 is inserted. How many probes does it take?
items.s: The occupied run holds 1 positions, so the key probes those 1 and then the free one, taking 2 probes in all.

items.q: A breadth first search starts at a vertex that has 6 neighbours, and every later vertex also has 6 neighbours. How many vertices stand on level 2 of the search?
items.s: The front grows by the factor 6 - 1 at each step, so level 2 holds 6 x 5^1 = 30 vertices.

items.q: A partition about a pivot leaves 1 items to the left of the pivot and 38 to its right in an array of 40 items. The right part is then sorted by a method that compares every pair once. How many comparisons does that part need?
items.s: The right part holds 38 items, so its pair comparisons number m(m-1)/2 = 703.

items.q: Quick sort takes its worst case on an array of 200 items already in order when the pivot is always the first item. How many comparisons are made?
items.s: Each partition removes one item and compares it with all the rest, giving n(n-1)/2 = 19900.

items.q: The unmodified recursive method for the 15th Fibonacci number makes one call for each node of its recursion tree. How many calls does it make in all?
items.s: The tree has 2 x F(16) - 1 nodes, and F(16) = 987, so the calls number 1973.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: A file of 100 items is sorted at a cost of n log2 n comparisons and then searched 10 times by binary search. Taking log2 100 as 6 and the cost of one binary search as 7 comparisons, how many comparisons are made in all?
items.s: The sort costs 100 x 6 = 600 comparisons and the searches cost 10 x 7 = 70, giving 670 in all.

items.q: A method performs 5 basic operations for each item of an input of size 1000. How many operations does it carry out in all?
items.s: The work is 5 operations per item times 1000 items, that is 5000 operations.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A nested loop runs an inner block whose cost is 1 operations once for every ordered pair of items in an input of size 50. How many operations are carried out?
items.s: There are n squared = 2500 ordered pairs, each costing 1, so the total is 2500.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A divide and conquer method splits an input of size 1024 into halves, spends 4 operations on every item at each level and has 10 levels in all. How many operations does it perform?
items.s: One level costs 4 x 1024 = 4096 operations and there are 10 levels, giving 40960 operations.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: The naive method for multiplying two 25 by 25 matrices performs two operations for every triple of indices. How many operations does it perform?
items.s: There are n cubed = 15625 triples and two operations for each, so 31250 operations.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A method needs one 8 byte record for each of the 2000 items of its input. How much storage does the working copy occupy, in bytes?
items.s: The copy holds 2000 records of 8 bytes, that is 16000 bytes.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: An array of 4 byte elements begins at address 1000. What is the address of the element with index 16?
items.s: The address is base + index x element size = 1000 + 16 x 4 = 1064.

items.q: A two dimensional array with 27 rows and 26 columns of 2 byte elements is stored row by row starting at address 1000. What is the address of the element in row 10 and column 5?
items.s: Its position in the block is row x columns + column = 265, so the address is 1000 + 265 x 2 = 1530.

items.q: A singly linked chain holds 2000 nodes, each carrying a 12 byte item and a pointer of 4 bytes. How many bytes of storage does the chain occupy?
items.s: Each node takes 12 + 4 = 16 bytes, so 2000 nodes take 32000 bytes.

items.q: A doubly linked chain holds 2500 nodes, each carrying a 32 byte item and two pointers of 4 bytes. How many bytes of storage does the chain occupy?
items.s: Each node takes 32 + 8 = 40 bytes, so the whole chain takes 100000 bytes.

items.q: A chain of 500 nodes is walked from the head to the node in position 100, counting the head as position one. How many nodes are passed through?
items.s: The walk stops at position 100 having passed through exactly 100 nodes.

items.q: An item is to be inserted into a sorted array of 1000 elements at index 53. How many existing elements must be moved one place to the right?
items.s: Every element from index 53 onwards shifts, which is 1000 - 53 = 947 elements.

items.q: A simulation performs 400 operations; 60 per cent of them push and the rest pop. How many pushes occur?
items.s: The pushes are 60/100 x 400 = 240 operations.

items.q: A circular queue uses 20 cells and its rear index currently stands at 19. After 3 further insertions, which index holds the rear?
items.s: Each insertion advances the index by one and wraps at 20, so (19 + 3) mod 20 = 2.

items.q: A stack is held in a block of 400 bytes and each item occupies 4 bytes. How many items can it hold?
items.s: The block holds 400/4 = 100 items.

items.q: The postfix expression 8 8 + is evaluated with a stack. What result is left on the stack?
items.s: The two values are pushed and the operator + combines them, giving 8 + 8 = 16.

items.q: A binary tree of height 10 is as full as it can be at every level. What is the largest number of nodes it can contain, counting the root as level one?
items.s: A full tree of height h holds 2^h - 1 nodes, so 2^10 - 1 = 1023.

items.q: In a full binary tree numbered with the root at level one, how many nodes stand on level 2?
items.s: Level one has one node and every level doubles the count, so level 2 holds 2^1 = 2 nodes.

items.q: A balanced binary search tree holds 7 keys. What is the greatest number of nodes examined by one lookup?
items.s: The search follows one node per level, and a balanced tree of 7 keys has 3 levels.

items.q: A binary heap is stored in an array with the root at index 0. What is the index of the parent of the node at index 166?
items.s: The parent of index i sits at (i - 1)/2 rounded down, so (166 - 1)/2 = 82.

items.q: A binary heap is stored in an array with the root at index 0. What is the index of the right child of the node at index 20?
items.s: The left child sits at 2i + 1 and the right at 2i + 2, so 2 x 20 + 2 = 42.

items.q: Keys are placed in a table of 17 positions by taking the remainder of the key on division by 17. At which position does the key 2500 land?
items.s: The remainder of 2500 on division by 17 is 1.

items.q: A hash table has 100 positions and holds 30 keys. Calculate its load factor.
items.s: The load factor is keys divided by positions: 30/100 = 0.3.

items.q: A hash table with 100 positions uses chaining and holds 500 keys. Taking the keys as evenly spread as possible, what is the average chain length?
items.s: The keys are shared among 100 positions, so each chain holds 500/100 = 5 keys on average.

items.q: A table holds 75 keys and the load factor must not exceed 50 per cent. What is the smallest number of positions that will serve?
items.s: The positions needed satisfy keys/positions at most 50/100, so at least 75 x 100/50 = 150 positions are required.

items.q: A chained hash table holds 1000 keys, each key takes 4 bytes and each chain pointer takes 8 bytes. How many bytes do the key records occupy in all?
items.s: Each record takes 4 + 8 = 12 bytes, so 1000 records take 12000 bytes.

items.q: An undirected graph has 25 vertices and no two are joined by more than one edge. What is the largest number of edges it can have?
items.s: Every vertex can reach the other n - 1, so the edges number 25 x 24 / 2 = 300.

items.q: An undirected graph with 500 vertices and 100 edges is stored as adjacency lists, each link taking 8 bytes and each list header taking 8 bytes. How many bytes are needed?
items.s: There are 500 headers and 2 x 100 = 200 links, so the total is 4000 + 1600 = 5600 bytes.

items.q: A spanning tree is to be formed for a connected graph with 250 vertices. How many edges does the tree contain?
items.s: A tree on 250 vertices always has one edge fewer than vertices, that is 249.

items.q: A graph has 8 vertices and every vertex has degree 3. How many edges does the graph contain?
items.s: The degrees total 8 x 3 = 24, and each edge is counted twice, so there are 12 edges.

items.q: Bubble sort is applied to an array of 100 items that happens to be in reverse order, so no pass ends early. How many comparisons are made?
items.s: The passes compare 100 - 1, then 100 - 2 and so on, which adds to n(n-1)/2 = 4950.

items.q: Selection sort is applied to an array of 25 items. How many comparisons does it make, whatever the original order?
items.s: The first scan compares 25 items, the next 24, and so on, giving n(n-1)/2 = 300.

items.q: Insertion sort is applied to an array of 20 items arranged in decreasing order. How many shifts of elements are carried out?
items.s: The worst case shifts 1 + 2 + ... + (20 - 1) elements, which is n(n-1)/2 = 190.

items.q: Merge sort is applied to 128 items. Into how many levels of splitting does the recursion divide the work?
items.s: The array is halved until single items remain, which takes log2(128) = 7 levels.

items.q: Merge sort is applied to 128 items and every level of the recursion does at most 128 comparisons in all. What is the largest total number of comparisons?
items.s: Each of the 7 levels costs at most 128 comparisons, so the total is at most 896.

items.q: A sorting method performs n log2 n comparisons on 5000 items. Taking log2 5000 as 12, how many comparisons does it perform?
items.s: The work is 5000 x 12 = 60000 comparisons.

items.q: A radix sort processes 100 keys and each key is examined once for each of its 3 digits. How many key examinations does the method make?
items.s: Every pass looks at all 100 keys, and there are 3 passes, so 300 examinations are made.

items.q: Binary search is applied to a sorted array of 31 items. What is the greatest number of comparisons it can make?
items.s: Each comparison halves the range, and the least k with 2^k at least 31 + 1 is 5.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: A recursive method makes 3 calls from every activation and the recursion has depth 6. Counting the first call as level zero, how many activations are created in all?
items.s: The levels hold 1, 3, 3 squared and so on up to 3^6, which adds to 1093 activations.
items.t: Searching, recursion and divide and conquer

items.q: A table of the smallest numbers of coins for every amount up to 30 is filled one amount at a time. How many entries are filled?
items.s: The amounts from one to 30 each take one entry, so 30 entries are filled.

items.q: A dynamic programming method for choosing items keeps one row for the empty choice and one row for each of 10 items, and one column for zero capacity and one for each of 4 capacity units. How many cells does the table hold?
items.s: The table has 10 + 1 = 11 rows and 4 + 1 = 5 columns, so it holds 55 cells.

items.q: A table of 32 positions uses linear probing. The positions from 9 through 17 are already occupied and the one after them is free. A key whose home position is 9 is inserted. How many probes does it take?
items.s: The occupied run holds 9 positions, so the key probes those 9 and then the free one, taking 10 probes in all.

items.q: A breadth first search starts at a vertex that has 3 neighbours, and every later vertex also has 3 neighbours. How many vertices stand on level 2 of the search?
items.s: The front grows by the factor 3 - 1 at each step, so level 2 holds 3 x 2^1 = 6 vertices.

items.q: A partition about a pivot leaves 3 items to the left of the pivot and 196 to its right in an array of 200 items. The right part is then sorted by a method that compares every pair once. How many comparisons does that part need?
items.s: The right part holds 196 items, so its pair comparisons number m(m-1)/2 = 19110.

items.q: A method performs 4 basic operations for each item of an input of size 1000. How many operations does it carry out in all?
items.s: The work is 4 operations per item times 1000 items, that is 4000 operations.
items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A nested loop runs an inner block whose cost is 4 operations once for every ordered pair of items in an input of size 40. How many operations are carried out?

items.t: Algorithm analysis and growth of functions

items.q: A divide and conquer method splits an input of size 128 into halves, spends 5 operations on every item at each level and has 7 levels in all. How many operations does it perform?
items.s: One level costs 5 x 128 = 640 operations and there are 7 levels, giving 4480 operations.

items.q: A method needs one 16 byte record for each of the 500 items of its input. How much storage does the working copy occupy, in bytes?
items.s: The copy holds 500 records of 16 bytes, that is 8000 bytes.

items.q: A two dimensional array with 8 rows and 11 columns of 2 byte elements is stored row by row starting at address 0. What is the address of the element in row 7 and column 6?

items.q: A singly linked chain holds 100 nodes, each carrying a 12 byte item and a pointer of 4 bytes. How many bytes of storage does the chain occupy?

items.q: A chain of 5000 nodes is walked from the head to the node in position 500, counting the head as position one. How many nodes are passed through?

the exploration of a graph by following one route as far as possible before backing up
